label: <DEL> step when the first two original tokens are both from a letter set {w,n,e,r,z,l,x,k,g,y,s,t}
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (98.8% of activation mass; about 12% of <DEL> steps), where the model is about to output original token 0. Never fires in the copy phase; a small residue (about 1% of mass) sits late in the original phase, mostly on input j. Which delimiters fire depends on the content of the first original tokens: the first token (out_tok = first_tok) matters most, with w highest (8x lift), then n, e, r, z, l, x, k. The second token (next_out) is the next biggest factor with a similar ordering (w, r, k, n, e, l, x). Requiring both tokens to come from the set {w,n,e,r,z,l,x,k,g,y,s,t} gives dev F1 0.66 and mass recall 0.85. Looks like a graded additive score rather than a crisp rule: magnitude is highest when the first two tokens are both w (the top examples start w w / w e / w e w), it rises with L (t = 9 holds the most mass), and it is mildly suppressed by digits among the originals. Does not fire on delimiters whose first token is a digit or a low-weight letter such as a, b, c, d.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, n, e, r, l, z; least: p, j, 3, i) and the second original token (most: w, r, e, k, n, l; least: p, 3, i, j); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, t=4.
